panels.sample_scope: Supplementary Fig. 10 | Sensitivity of paired environmental contrasts to sampling centre. Temporary-minus-final contrasts use three centres: the observed position at every lag, the fixed departure position, and a mixed centre fixed before departure and following the cyclone afterwards. a–f, RH (a), PI − V (b), PI (c), signed entropy ratio χ (d), its signed entropy-deficit numerator (e) and signed ventilation  (f). The entropy deficit compares saturated 600-hPa core entropy at 0–100 km with environmental entropy at 100–300 km around the same centre; χ divides this deficit by surface-to-boundary-layer entropy disequilibrium. Negative signed values are retained. “Pre” averages −24, −18, −12 and −6 h with at least three common lags; “Change” is +24 h minus departure. Each variable uses a common finite SID–lag mask across events and centre comparisons. RH has n=117 for pre-means and n=105 for changes; the thermodynamic quantities have n=58 and n=53. Cells give the mean contrast in native units. Each physical variable has an independent zero-centred colour scale; colour magnitudes should be compared within a panel. Table S5h reports all 36 estimates, sample sizes and pointwise 95% percentiles from 2,000 paired-cyclone resamples. Pre-mean and change summaries use their respective eligible samples and do not imply identical support across windows. Positive values indicate larger temporary-departure values or subsequent changes. The mixed-centre definition yields identical fixed/mixed pre-means and along-track/mixed changes.
